source.title: Representational Capacity: Geometric Limits on Feature Representation in Transformer Language Models

record.tranche_reason: Tests the geometric packing component of superposition using optimized vector sets and an embedding-based proxy, but does not reproduce sparse-feature toy networks.
record.gate_note: The paper directly measures embedding similarities across models and optimizes synthetic vector sets. The embedding results are not measurements of feature directions, sparse activations, neuron polysemanticity, or SAE recovery. The synthetic vector sweep has no network, feature-activation, sparsity, or importance mechanism. Cited SAE feature counts are not new results here.
record.test_reason: The paper takes superposition as a premise and builds a capacity bound from it. Its own results do not bear on any version. The synthetic sweep optimizes bare unit-vector sets (no network, no sparse features, no importance, no sparsity transition), so it is a packing-geometry fit, not a toy model of feature storage (V1). The LLM results are cosine-similarity statistics of token embedding matrices. They are not measurements of features spread across neurons or of SAE recovery (V4), and the authors say extending them to features is an unverified hypothesis. The SAE feature counts it uses are cited, not new.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that embedding ε splits models into two classes, with high-ε models not using superposition at the embedding level. They report that standard JL badly underestimates packing and that a k/d form fixes this. They find capacity exponentially sensitive to ε, and larger models favoring tighter orthogonality, with the cause left open. They stress that capacity bounds geometric possibility, not realized feature use, and that the embedding-to-feature extension is a hypothesis.
record.recipe_differences: Uses embedding cosine statistics and optimized vector arrangements rather than the original toy-network sparse-feature setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Embedding/unembedding tying is associated with the high-ε class; capacity estimates vary strongly with ε and dmodel. The paper notes the embedding-to-feature generalization is unverified.

fits_no_version.finding: Token-embedding cosine-similarity spread (ε = µ+2σ) splits 45 models into a high-ε class (ε>0.2, mostly tied embeddings) and a low-ε class (ε<0.1). Within the low-ε class, larger dmodel goes with smaller ε.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Near-orthogonality of token embeddings varies by model class (associated with embedding tying) and tightens with dmodel. This is an embedding-geometry property, not a direct measure of feature superposition.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient-optimized unit-vector sets pack far more ε-near-orthogonal directions than the JL random bound. The max pairwise similarity fits ε≈sqrt(C·ln(k/d)/d) with C≈1.293, R2=0.9984, versus MAPE≈975% for standard JL.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimized (non-random) vector arrangements achieve packing capacity scaling as d·exp(dε²/C), exceeding JL estimates for random projections.

record.problems: The ε threshold is heuristic; the extension from embeddings to latent features is explicitly unproven; optimized vectors are synthetic and do not model feature sparsity or network learning; capacity is geometric possibility rather than measured utilization; the paper notes limited data at larger model dimensions.

untested.parts: Small networks trained on sparse features, the sparsity-dependent transition, feature importance, and the learned geometry. Only bare optimized vector packing is studied.
Neuron polysemanticity, and dedicated versus shared dimensions by feature importance.
Feature spread across neurons and SAE recovery in LLMs. Only embedding-matrix cosine statistics are measured, and SAE counts are cited.
SAE feature completeness, stability, and canonicity.
Feature dimensionality. Features are assumed to be 1-D directions, not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 'supports' label was removed: the optimized-vector sweep has no network or sparse features and is the authors' own formula fit. Table 1 values spot-checked and match. Llama 2 70B (ε=0.09962, capacity 8.15e15) is flagged by the authors as an outlier. Gemma 7B ε≈1 is an extreme outlier.

versions.untested_parts: Tests optimized near-orthogonal vector packing, not feature storage in small networks, sparse co-activation, sparsity-dependent transitions, feature importance, or regular network geometries.
No measurement of neuron polysemanticity, feature importance, or dedicated versus shared neuron capacity.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Embedding similarities are measured, but feature spread across neurons and SAE recovery in LLMs are not measured.
No test of SAE feature completeness, stability, or canonical status.
Features are discussed as directions, but feature dimensionality is not measured.

rows.subject: random unit vectors
rows.operation_detail: Fit the standard JL relationship to random-vector trials; T = 1000 trials per (k, d).
rows.note: A fit to random vectors, not a test of feature storage in a network.
rows.check: This is a JL-constant fit to random unit vectors, a methodological calibration rather than a measurement of superposed features in a network. It should not link to V1.

rows.subject: optimized vectors
rows.operation_detail: Fit the standard JL relationship to optimized vector sets.

conditions.value: Minimize high-exponent off-diagonal Gram-matrix penalty; 5,000 steps

rows.note: Reports failure of this fit to optimized-vector data; it does not measure features.
rows.check: This reports the fit error of the standard JL form on optimized vector sets with no network or sparse features. It does not measure V1's feature storage.

rows.subject: optimized vectors
rows.operation_detail: Fit adjusted relationship replacing ln(k) with ln(k/d).

conditions.value: Minimize high-exponent off-diagonal Gram-matrix penalty; 5,000 steps

rows.measure: R2, MAPE, and reduction in MAPE versus standard JL.
rows.baseline: Standard JL on optimized data: MAPE ≈ 975%.
rows.note: Supports an empirical packing relation for optimized vector sets, but not feature storage by sparse networks.
rows.check: The authors' adjusted k/d formula is their own method's fit quality versus standard JL on synthetic vectors. It is not evidence on V1's toy-network superposition.

rows.subject: optimized vectors
rows.operation_detail: Fit fully parameterized adjusted relationship to optimized vector sets.

conditions.value: Minimize high-exponent off-diagonal Gram-matrix penalty; 5,000 steps

rows.note: A fit to synthetic vector arrangements, not to feature representations.
rows.check: This compares the authors' own formula variants on synthetic vectors. It is not a measure of any version.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Optimized synthetic vector sets in the tested dimension and vector-count sweep
reader_labels.reason: The adjusted k/d relationship fits the optimized vector packing data substantially better than the standard JL form (OPT2–OPT4); this supports the geometric-packing component only, not sparse-feature storage by networks.
